paper_title: Bridging Cognition and Emotion Empathy-Driven Multimodal Misinformation   Detection
caption: Results of Ablation Study
model_annotation: The bar chart, titled "Results of Ablation Study" and associated with the paper "Bridging Cognition and Emotion Empathy-Driven Multimodal Misinformation Detection," compares the accuracy (%) of a model under different experimental conditions across two datasets: PHEME and PolitiFact. The vertical axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 75.0 to 95.0 with a scale of 2.5. The horizontal axis displays the model configurations, which are categorized by the presence or absence of specific features: "Ours" (the full model), "w/o comments," "w/o text," "w/o select," "w/o emotion," and "w/o cognition." The chart is divided into two main sections by a vertical line. On the PHEME dataset, the "Ours" model achieves the highest accuracy at 89.84%, followed by "w/o comments" at 86.82%, "w/o select" at 88.80%, "w/o emotion" at 87.34%, "w/o cognition" at 87.17%, and "w/o text" at 80.10%. On the PolitiFact dataset, the "Ours" model again shows the highest accuracy at 90.57%, followed by "w/o select" at 89.62%, "w/o comments" at 85.85%, "w/o emotion" at 84.91, "w/o cognition" at 87.74%, and "w/o text" at 83.02%. The bars are color-coded: dark red for "Ours," orange for "w/o comments," light yellow for "w/o text," light blue for "w/o select," medium blue for "w/o emotion," and dark blue for "w/o cognition." The results indicate that the full model performs best on both datasets, and removing the "w/o text" feature leads to the most significant drop in accuracy.
